algorithm.nochatreports.aes_cfb8_base64:
§lAES/CFB8+Base64R§r
Standard symmetric encryption algorithm. Uses 128 bit keys, output is encoded in a special version of Base64 to permit transfer via Minecraft's chat. As a downside - messages will gain roughly 30% increase in length and the server might truncate them if they exceed the size limit.
algorithm.nochatreports.aes_ecb_base64:
§lAES/ECB+Base64R§r
Considerably less secure than CFB mode, but saves you some bytes by not requiring the initialization vector. Still beats Caesar.
algorithm.nochatreports.aes_gcm_base64:
§lAES/GCM+Base64R§r
More security in exchange for a severe increase in message size (12 bytes for the initialization vector and 12 bytes for the authentication tag, Base64 encoding on top). Choose this if you value security over anything else.
algorithm.nochatreports.caesar:
§lCaesar§r
Meme cipher. With this you're basically hoping that people will give up without even trying to decrypt your messages. That might be true in many cases, so the viability of using it depends on your threat model.
The key should be an integer from 1 to 1024. The shift is done by character code instead of alphabetically to ensure compatibility with any language.

block.redstonepen.control_box.help.1:
§nBasics:§r§7 The RLC provides digital (ON/OFF) and analog
§7(signal strength, comparator output) redstone I/O
§7in all directions. Ports are the first letters of: Red,
§7Blue, Yellow, Green, Up, and Down.
§7You program it with a set of math expressions. All code 
§7lines are calculated in the same tick (read inputs ->
§7calculate -> write outputs). The code is case insensitive
§7("R" is the same as "r"). You can also set own variables,
§7their values will be retained until the RLC is stopped.
§7Parse errors are marked (hover that) and prevent
§7to start the program.

§7Click the RUN/STOP button to start or stop a program.
§7Hover the RLC symbol to see internal variable values
§7(only when running). The port list shows the current
§7signal values, and if a port is input, output, or unused.
§7Copy/paste clipboard button, needless to say ;)
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.10:
§nFurther:§r§7 The Control normally calculates every 4 ticks,
§7when an input port changes form ON->OFF or OFF->ON,
§7the run cycle is re-scheduled to the next possible tick.
§7Assign the "TICKRATE" variable to alter the base tickrate
§7between 2t and 20t.
§7
§7Comparator inputs do not trigger this scheduling.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.2:
§nExpressions§r§7 are stated like "RESULT=TERM" assignments,
§7e.g. "R = G & B". Every code line must be like that.
§7Use a "#" to mark the rest of a line as comment.
§7The TERM can consist of parentheses "(...)", ports,
§7variables, operators, and functions.

§7If you assign to a port variable (R, B, Y, G, U, D), it is
§7automatically set as output, and input signal changes
§7are ignored there. If you use a port variable (that is
§7not already output) in an expression, it is automatically
§7set to input.
§7Comparator-Outputs of adjacent blocks are read with
§7the ".CO" suffix. E.g. "Y = MAX( B.CO, R, g.co, MyVar )".
§7CO's are never RLC outputs, even if you assign them.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.3:
§nArithmetic§r§7 is Integer arithmetic in the RLC, means
§7"A * 1.5" is not accepted, and divisions are rounded
§7toward zero. Supported operations are:

§7  "+", "-", "*", "/", "%" (latter is modulo division).

§7Variable assignments hold any positive or negative
§732bit integer value (bigger than you need).
§7Port values however are implicitly clamped to the
§7valid redstone value range 0..15.
§7Int32 wrap-over applies, division-by-zero yields
§70 and a singularity to the Dungeon Dimensions.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.4:
§nRelational§r§7 operators provide numeric comparisons:
§7
§7  "==" (equal), "!=" (not equal),
§7  ">=" (greater-equal), "<=" (less-equal),
§7  ">" (greater-than), "<" (less-than).
§7
§7They evaluate to 0 if the comparison result is
§7"false", and 15 if "true". As the values are numbers,
§7you can directly calculate with them. E.g. "G=(R>11)/3"
§7results in 5 or 0. However, better would be instead
§7using the IF function: "G = IF( R>11, 5, 0 )".
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.5:
§nLogical§r§7 operations work with "Redstone Boolean" values,
§7which are integral numbers. Operands that are greater
§7than 0 are considered "true". The operations yield 0 for
§7"false" and 15 for "true". Supported are:
§7
§7 AND: "AND", "&&", "&"
§7 OR: "OR", "||", "|"
§7 XOR: "XOR", "^"
§7 NOT: "NOT", "!"
§7
§7Rule of thumb: The OPs see inputs like a Redstone Lamp
§7and yield outputs like a Lever. Coders: There are no
§7bitwise operations.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.6:
§nEdge Detection§r§7 means tracking of inputs the moment they
§7change from OFF [0] to ON [>0] and vice versa.
§7Rising edge triggers are set up with the ".RE" suffix, and
§7are 15 for one tick when the input changes from OFF to ON.
§7Falling edge triggers are set up with the ".FE" suffix, and
§7are 15 for one tick when the input changes from ON to OFF.
§7E.g:
§7
§7 C = C+IF(R.RE OR G.FE OR Y.CO.RE, 1, 0) # Count C up
§7 C = CNT1(G.RE, B.RE, 10) # Using up-down-counter1
§7
§7Notes: Although the RLC may not execute every tick, edges
§7are still detected on input ports ("interrupt"). The PLC
§7equivalents are called RTRIG and FTRIG.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.7:
§nTimers§r§7 in PLCs are signal based. The dominant three
§7are implemented in the RLC: TON, TOF, and TP:
§7TON is a Switch-On-Delay. The input signal must be steadily
§7ON for a specified time, after which the timer output rises
§7to ON. Any OFF-signal resets the timer immediately. TOF is
§7the same inverted (Switch-Off-Delay). TP generates a pulse
§7for a specified time when seeing a rising edge of the input
§7signal. Any signal change during the pulse is ignored.
§7The RLC has 5 (simplified) instances of each type:
§7
§7 A = TON3( INPUT_TERM, ON_DELAY_TICKS )
§7 A = TOF2( INPUT_TERM, OFF_DELAY_TICKS )
§7 A = TP4( INPUT_TERM, PULSE_TIME_TICKS )
§7 R = TON1( Y.CO<3, 30*20 ) # Hopper low alarm after 30s
§7 R = TP1( Y.RE, 20 ) # Observer pulse extension 1s.

§7The timer settings (PT) can be changed while the timers
§7are active.
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.8:
§nCounters§r§7 help keeping track of event occurrences. The RLC
§7has five up-down counters CNT1..5 with optional input
§7arguments:
§7
§7N = CNTx(Iup)   # Count up if Iup is >0
§7N = CNTx(Iup, Idown)   # IDown>0: Count back to 0
§7N = CNTx(Iup, Idown, Max)   # Count 0..Max
§7N = CNTx(Iup, Idown, Min, Max)   # Count Min..Max
§7N = CNTx(Iup, Idown, Min, Max, Reset)    # Reset to Min
§7
§7N holds the new counter value. Note: For event counting use
§7signal edges (e.g. G.RE) as inputs. Counters are not guaranteed
§7tick time accurate (use timers for timing).
block.redstonepen.control_box.help.9:
§nFunction Reference§r
§7IF(X,A,B)   # A if X>0 else B
§7INV(X)   # Redstone invert: 15-X, result 0..15.
§7MAX(A,B,...), MIN(...), MEAN(...)   # Min, max, average
§7LIM(X), LIM(X,B), LIM(X,A,B)   # Limit 0..15, 0..B, A..B
§7TIME(), CLOCK()    # Day time, game time
§7RND()   # Random 0..15
§7
§7§nRLC specific function blocks§r
§7
§7TIVx(T) # Interval, pulse every T ticks (TIV1/TIV2/TIV3)§r
§7TIVx(T, EN) # Interval, pulse every T ticks if ENable set.
§7# (Minimum interval is 3 ticks).

constructionstick.description.stick:
The %s can place up to %s blocks at the side of a building facing you and lasts %s.

Press the bound %s key to change placement restriction (Horizontal, Vertical, North/South, East/West, No lock).

Open the option screen with the bound %s key.

§5§nUNDO§0§r
Holding down the bound %s key while looking at a blocks will show you the last blocks you placed with a green border around them. Pressing the bound %s key while looking at any of them will undo the operation, giving you all the items back. If you used the Destruction upgrade, it will restore the blocks.

§5§nCONTAINERS§0§r
Shulker boxes, bundles and many containers from other mods can provide building blocks for the stick.

§5§nOFFHAND PRIORITY§0§r
Having blocks in your offhand will place them instead of the block you're looking at.
constructionstick.description.upgrade:
§5§nINSTALLATION§0§r
Put your new upgrade template together with your stick and the required item in a Smithing Table to apply (Check the Smithing Table recipes to see the required item). To switch between upgrades, press the bound %s key while holding your stick or use the option screen.

fancymenu.actions.audio.set_audio_elemen:

fancymenu.actions.download_file.desc:
This action downloads a file from a URL and saves it to the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

Provide the download folder instead of a file name; FancyMenu derives the saved file name from the HTTP response headers or the URL automatically.

§lAsynchronous Download:§r This action downloads files asynchronously, which means the download happens in the background without freezing or blocking the game. The game will continue running normally while the file is being downloaded.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

In this mode, the element's position will get calculated

are also cases where this behaviour is not optimal.

fancymenu.listeners.on_animated_texture_:
This listener triggers when an animated texture (GIF, APNG or FMA) finishes a playback cycle. If the texture loops, it fires right before the animation restarts.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$texture_source §r= The source of the texture (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$texture_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$texture_will_restart §r= TRUE if the texture will restart after this cycle, otherwise FALSE

This listener triggers when an animated texture (GIF, APNG or FMA) starts playing. It also triggers when the texture restarts because of looping.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$texture_source §r= The source of the texture (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$texture_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$texture_will_restart §r= TRUE if the texture will restart after this cycle, otherwise FALSE
fancymenu.listeners.on_block_broke.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player breaks a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the broken block
- §z$$broke_with_item_key §r= The resource location of the item/tool that was used (or EMPTY when nothing was held)
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the broken block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the broken block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the broken block
fancymenu.listeners.on_block_placed.desc:

- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the placed block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the placed block

fancymenu.listeners.on_chat_message_rece:
Triggers whenever the client displays a normal player chat message.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$chat_message_component §r= Full component JSON of the received chat line
- §z$$sender_uuid §r= UUID of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)
- §z$$sender_name §r= Plain name of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)

fancymenu.listeners.on_damage_taken.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player takes damage.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$damage_amount §r= The amount of health removed by the hit
- §z$$damage_type §r= The resource location of the damage type
- §z$$is_fatal_damage §r= TRUE when the hit reduced the player to zero health
- §z$$damage_source §r= The resource location of the entity that caused the damage or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.listeners.on_death.desc:
Triggers right after the vanilla death screen opens for the local player.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$days_survived §r= In-game days survived (rounded down) since the last death
- §z$$death_reason_string §r= Plain text description of the death reason
- §z$$death_reason_component §r= Full component JSON of the death reason
- §z$$death_pos_x §r= X coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= Y coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_z §r= Z coordinate where the player died

fancymenu.listeners.on_effect_gained.des:

- §z$$effect_type §r= The effect category (positive, negative, neutral)
- §z$$effect_duration §r= The effect duration in ticks remaining
fancymenu.listeners.on_effect_lost.desc:

fancymenu.listeners.on_element_spawned.d:
This listener triggers when an element instance is spawned via the 'Spawn Element Instance' action.

- §z$$element_identifier §r= The spawned element's identifier

fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_biome.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player enters a new biome.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$biome_key §r= The resource location of the biome the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.d:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player enters a structure using coarse structure-area detection.

Because it considers the entire structure footprint, it can also fire when a structure is near or below the player (for example, a mineshaft beneath the surface).

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.h:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player actually steps into a structure's interior.

It uses high precision detection, so it only fires when the player enters the structure's bounding boxes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_died.desc:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers whenever an entity dies anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that died
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the death position (returns -1 when the entity died in another dimension)
- §z$$death_pos_x §r= The X coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate where the entity died

- §z$$dimension_key §r= The dimension the entity died in
- §z$$damage_type §r= The resource location of the damage type that caused the death
- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity died in the same dimension as the player
- §z$$entity_killed_by_name §r= The plain text name of the killer or NONE when unavailable
- §z$$entity_killed_by_key §r= The resource location of the killer's type (uses minecraft:player for players, NONE when unavailable)
- §z$$entity_killed_by_uuid §r= The UUID of the killer or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_in_sight.d:
This listener triggers once when an entity first becomes visible in the player's field of view (and is not farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the visible entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the visible entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_mounted.de:
This listener triggers once when the player begins riding an entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the mounted entity type
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate when mounting started
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate when mounting started
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate when mounting started
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the mounted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_spawned.de:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers whenever an entity spawns anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the spawned entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the spawn location (returns -1 when the entity spawned in another dimension)
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the spawned entity
- §z$$dimension_key §r= The dimension the entity spawned in
- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity spawned in the same dimension as the player
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_starts_bei:
This listener triggers once when an entity first becomes visible in the player's field of view (and is not farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the visible entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the visible entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_stops_bein:
This listener triggers once when an entity that was previously visible in the player's field of view stops being visible (or moves farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that just left the view
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that just left the view
This listener triggers once when the player stops riding their current entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity that was dismounted
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate when dismounting
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate when dismounting
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate when dismounting
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that was dismounted
fancymenu.listeners.on_experience_change:
This listener triggers whenever the player's total experience amount changes (gaining or losing XP).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$new_experience_amount §r= The player's total experience value after the change
- §z$$old_experience_amount §r= The player's total experience value before the change
- §z$$is_level_up §r= TRUE when the change increased the player's level
fancymenu.listeners.on_file_downloaded.d:
This listener triggers when a file finishes downloading via the 'Download File to Game Directory' action.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$download_url §r= The URL of the file that got downloaded
- §z$$target_file_path §r= The path the file got saved to
- §z$$download_succeeded §r= If the file download was successful (true/false)
fancymenu.listeners.on_file_selected.des:
This listener triggers after the 'Select File' action finishes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$selected_file_path §r= The absolute path of the chosen file (empty when the dialog was cancelled)
- §z$$target_file_path §r= The resolved path inside the Minecraft instance that received the file
- §z$$selection_succeeded §r= 'true' when the file was copied successfully
- §z$$selection_cancelled §r= 'true' when the dialog was closed without selecting a file
- §z$$failure_reason §r= Error information when the action failed
This listener triggers when the server sends FMData to this client via '/fmdata send'.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$data_identifier §r= The identifier string that was sent with the data
- §z$$data §r= The data payload string that was sent
- §z$$sent_by §r= The server IP that sent the data, or 'integrated_server' in singleplayer
fancymenu.listeners.on_interacted_with_b:
This listener triggers once when the player successfully interacts with a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the interacted block
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the block
fancymenu.listeners.on_interacted_with_e:
This listener triggers once when the player successfully interacts with an entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the interacted entity type
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate at the time of interaction
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate at the time of interaction
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate at the time of interaction
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the interacted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_broke.desc:
This listener triggers once when an item in the player's inventory breaks.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the broken item
- §z$$item_type §r= Category of the broken item (tool, armor, other)
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_consumed.des:
This listener triggers once when the player finishes consuming an item.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the item that was consumed
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_dropped.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player drops an item from their inventory.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the item that was dropped
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_hovered_in_i:
This listener triggers once when the player starts hovering an item in any inventory (player inventory, chest, etc.).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the hovered item
- §z$$item_display_name_string §r= The plain text display name of the hovered item
- §z$$item_display_name_json §r= The serialized raw JSON text component of the hovered item
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_picked_up.de:
This listener triggers once when the player picks up an item entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the item that was picked up
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_used.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player uses an item.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$item_key §r= The resource location of the item that was used
- §z$$used_on_type §r= The interaction context (block, entity, self, none)
- §z$$used_on_entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that was targeted, empty when none
- §z$$used_on_block_key §r= The resource location of the block that was targeted, empty when none
- §z$$target_pos_x §r= Target X position when available, otherwise -1
- §z$$target_pos_y §r= Target Y position when available, otherwise -1
- §z$$target_pos_z §r= Target Z position when available, otherwise -1
fancymenu.listeners.on_key_pressed.desc:
This listener triggers whenever a keyboard key is pressed, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server). The listener keeps firing while the key is held down and the screen continues to receive repeat events.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$key_name §r= The resolved display name of the key
- §z$$key_keycode §r= The GLFW key code
- §z$$key_scancode §r= The GLFW scan code
- §z$$key_modifiers §r= The active modifier bit mask
fancymenu.listeners.on_key_released.desc:
This listener triggers whenever a keyboard key is released, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$key_name §r= The resolved display name of the key
- §z$$key_keycode §r= The GLFW key code
- §z$$key_scancode §r= The GLFW scan code
- §z$$key_modifiers §r= The active modifier bit mask
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_biome.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player leaves their current biome.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$biome_key §r= The resource location of the biome the player just left
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_structure.d:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player leaves their current structure using coarse structure-area detection.

Because it considers the entire structure footprint, it can also fire when a structure is near or below the player (for example, a mineshaft beneath the surface).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player just left
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_structure.h:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers once when the player leaves the interior of their current structure.

It uses high precision detection, so it only fires after the player fully exits the structure's bounding boxes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$structure_key §r= The resource location of the structure the player just left
This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at a block in the world.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the targeted block
- §z$$distance §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_button_clic:
This listener triggers once when a mouse button is pressed, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$button §r= Which button was pressed (left, right, middle)
- §z$$mouse_pos_x §r= The current mouse X position
- §z$$mouse_pos_y §r= The current mouse Y position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_button_rele:
This listener triggers once when a mouse button is released, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$button §r= Which button was released (left, right, middle)
- §z$$mouse_pos_x §r= The current mouse X position
- §z$$mouse_pos_y §r= The current mouse Y position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_moved.desc:
This listener triggers whenever the mouse cursor moves while a screen is open.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$mouse_pos_x §r= The current mouse X position
- §z$$mouse_pos_y §r= The current mouse Y position
- §z$$mouse_move_delta_x §r= The horizontal distance moved since the last event
- §z$$mouse_move_delta_y §r= The vertical distance moved since the last event
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_scrolled.de:
This listener triggers whenever the mouse wheel is scrolled while a screen is open.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$scroll_delta_y §r= The vertical scroll amount for the event
fancymenu.listeners.on_music_track_start:
This listener triggers once when a new music track starts playing.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$track_resource_location §r= The resolved resource location of the audio file that started
- §z$$track_display_name §r= Human-readable track name when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- §z$$track_artist §r= Reported track artist when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- §z$$track_duration_ms §r= Track duration expressed in milliseconds (0 when unknown)
fancymenu.listeners.on_music_track_stopp:
This listener triggers once when the current music track stops playing (naturally or because it was replaced).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$track_resource_location §r= The resolved resource location of the audio file that stopped
- §z$$track_display_name §r= Human-readable track name when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- §z$$track_artist §r= Reported track artist when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- §z$$track_duration_ms §r= Track duration expressed in milliseconds (0 when unknown)
fancymenu.listeners.on_open_screen.desc:
Triggers immediately after a screen becomes active, allowing actions such as "Open Screen or Custom GUI" to override it.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$screen_identifier §r= Identifier of the screen that just opened
fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_died:
Triggers when another player in the current world dies.

- §z$$player_uuid §r= The UUID of the player who died
- §z$$death_pos_x §r= X coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= Y coordinate where the player died
- §z$$death_pos_z §r= Z coordinate where the player died
fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_join:

fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_left:

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$player_name §r= The plain name of the player who left
- §z$$player_uuid §r= The UUID of the player who left
This listener triggers once whenever the local player's block position changes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$old_pos_y §r= Previous block Y coordinate
- §z$old_pos_z §r= Previous block Z coordinate
- §z$new_pos_x §r= New block X coordinate

fancymenu.listeners.on_quit_minecraft.de:

- §z$$timestamp_iso §r= ISO-8601 timestamp representing the quit moment
fancymenu.listeners.on_remote_server_con:

- §z$$intentionally_closed §r= TRUE if the close was triggered by a close action

- §z$$unknown_close_reason §r= TRUE if the connection closed unexpectedly without a known crash reason
fancymenu.listeners.on_remote_server_dat:
This listener triggers whenever text data is received from a connected remote server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$request_id §r= The request ID of the remote connection/message
- §z$$remote_server_url §r= The URL of the remote server connection
- §z$$data §r= The received text data payload
fancymenu.listeners.on_server_joined.des:
Triggers after the client finishes joining a multiplayer server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$server_ip §r= IP address of the server the player joined
fancymenu.listeners.on_server_left.desc:
Triggers after the client disconnects from a multiplayer server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$server_ip §r= IP address of the server the player left
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_looking_at_:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at a block in the world.

It only detects blocks within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the targeted block
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the targeted block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the targeted block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the targeted block
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position

This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at an entity.

It only detects entities within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the targeted entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the targeted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_swimming.de:
This listener triggers once when the player starts swimming.

- §z$$fluid_type §r= The resource location of the fluid the player started swimming in
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_touching_fl:
This listener triggers once when the player starts touching a fluid.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$fluid_type §r= The resource location of the fluid the player touched
This listener triggers once when the player starts freezing.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$freezing_intensity §r= The current freezing intensity (0.0 = no freeze, 1.0 = fully frozen)
fancymenu.listeners.on_stepping_on_block:
This listener triggers once when the player steps onto a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the block that was stepped on
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the block
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_looking_at_b:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair stops pointing at a block and reports information about the block that was previously targeted.

It only reports data for blocks that were within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$block_key §r= The resource location of the block that was targeted
- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the previously targeted block
- §z$$block_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate of the previously targeted block
- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the previously targeted block
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_looking_at_e:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair stops pointing at an entity and fires with information about the entity that was previously targeted.

It reports data for entities that were within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that was targeted
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that was targeted
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_swimming.des:
This listener triggers once when the player stops swimming.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$fluid_type §r= The resource location of the fluid the player stopped swimming in
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_touching_flu:
This listener triggers once when the player stops touching a fluid.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$fluid_type §r= The resource location of the fluid the player stopped touching
fancymenu.listeners.on_system_message_re:
Triggers whenever the client displays a system message in chat.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$system_message_string §r= Plain text version of the received message
- §z$$system_message_component §r= Full component JSON of the received message
fancymenu.listeners.on_text_clicked.desc:
This listener triggers when a click event in a Markdown text is clicked.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$text_event_id §r= The unique identifier from the click event markdown.
fancymenu.listeners.on_text_hovered.desc:
This listener triggers when a hover event in a Markdown text is hovered.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$text_event_id §r= The unique identifier from the hover event markdown.
This listener triggers whenever a FancyMenu variable gets updated/set.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$var_name §r= The variable name
- §z$$old_value §r= The old variable value
- §z$$new_value §r= The new variable value
fancymenu.listeners.on_video_playback_st:
This listener triggers whenever video playback state changes.

Possible values for §z$$new_status§r:
- PLAYING: Video started and is now playing (including when resuming from pause)
- STOPPED: Video was stopped through stop()
- PAUSED: Video was paused through pause()
- FINISHED: Video naturally reached the end of playback

If looping is enabled, FINISHED is emitted when the end is reached, right before the next loop starts.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$video_source §r= The source of the video (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$video_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$is_looping §r= TRUE if looping is enabled, otherwise FALSE
- §z$$new_status §r= New playback status (PLAYING, STOPPED, PAUSED, FINISHED)
fancymenu.listeners.on_weather_changed.d:
This listener triggers once whenever the weather state changes (clear, rain, or thunder).
It will also re-trigger when the local weather changes, which means if it is raining, for example, and you enter a biome that has no rain (desert) or a biome where it is snowing, the listener will re-trigger even though the global weather didn't change.
Entering a building also counts as local weather change while it is raining outside, because well, it doesn't rain inside.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$weather_type §r= The new global weather type (clear, rain, thunder)
- §z$$weather_can_snow §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as snow
- §z$$weather_can_rain §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as rain
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_entered.des:
Triggers after a singleplayer world finishes loading and the player regains control.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$world_name §r= Display name of the world
- §z$$world_save_path §r= Absolute path to the world save folder
- §z$$world_difficulty §r= Current game difficulty key
- §z$$world_cheats_allowed §r= TRUE when cheats are enabled
- §z$$world_icon_path §r= Absolute path to the world icon
- §z$$world_is_first_join §r= TRUE when this is the very first visit after creation
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_left.desc:
Triggers after a singleplayer world closes and finishes saving.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$world_name §r= Display name of the world
- §z$$world_save_path §r= Absolute path to the world save folder
- §z$$world_difficulty §r= Last known game difficulty key
- §z$$world_cheats_allowed §r= TRUE when cheats were enabled
- §z$$world_icon_path §r= Absolute path to the world icon
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_sound_trigg:
This listener triggers whenever a positional world sound starts playing near the player.

fancymenu.placeholders.nbt_data_get.desc:
Gets NBT data from entities and blocks (similar to '/data get' command).
Returns the value at the specified NBT path.

§lTIP: §rUse the '/data get' command in-game without setting a path
to easily get all available NBT paths for an entity or block!

Required values:
- source_type: The data source type ('entity' or 'block')
- nbt_path: The NBT path to query (e.g. 'foodLevel', 'Pos[0]', 'Inventory[0].id')

Conditional values:
- entity_selector: Entity selector when source_type is 'entity'
  Supports: @s (self), @p (nearest player), @e (nearest entity),
  UUID, or entity name
- block_pos: Block position when source_type is 'block'
  Format: 'x y z' (e.g. '100 64 -200')

Optional values:
- scale: Scale factor for numeric values (default: 1.0)
- return_type: How to return the data (default: 'value')
  Options: 'value' (numeric/size), 'string' (text value),
  'snbt' (formatted NBT), 'json' (JSON format)

Returns empty string if data cannot be accessed or path is invalid.
fancymenu.placeholders.nbt_data_get.serv:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

Fetches live NBT data from the server, mirroring every target supported by '/data get'.
Returns an empty value until the server response arrives.

The placeholder works exactly like the '/data get' command, so everything that should be possible with the command should also be possible with the placeholder.

Supported source_type values:
- entity: Full selector syntax (scores, advancements, predicates, rotation, gamemode, etc.)
- block: Absolute, relative (~) or local (^) coordinates like the vanilla command
- storage: Command storage identifiers (namespace:key)

Optional arguments:
- nbt_path: Same path rules as '/data get'
- scale: Multiplies numeric results (default 1.0)
- return_type: 'value', 'string', 'snbt', or 'json'

Responses are cached for 100ms to avoid spamming the server.

gui.tooltip.block.pneumaticcraft.advance:
This machine is the tier two version of the Air Compressor. Like its less resistant brother it can generate compressed air using any fuel that can burn in a Furnace. However, this one generates at 50mL/tick, and also produces heat. The higher the heat, the lower the efficiency. The bottom arrow in the temperature gauge indicates where the efficiency will start to drop, and the top arrow indicates the 0%% efficiency mark.

Unlike you might expect from this mod, this machine won't explode when the temperature gets too high.

The bottom arrow in the temperature gauge indicates where the efficiency will start to drop, and the top arrow indicates the 0%% efficiency mark.

Unlike you might expect from this mod, this machine won't explode when the temperature gets too high.
gui.tooltip.block.pneumaticcraft.elevato:
This machine is - like the name says - an elevator. You can use this to transport any entities. For it to work you'll need some air pressure and Elevator Frames on top of this block to support the elevator. To control the height level apply a redstone signal or use Elevator Callers. A redstone strength of 0 equals 0%% extension, a strength of 15 equals 100%% extension.

You can extend your elevators sideways. When you connect them in a way that the topmost Elevator Base for every elevator is at the same height, they will share the floor names/desired heights.

gui.tooltip.block.pneumaticcraft.flux_co:
Converts Forge Energy (compatible with RF and many other mods' energy) into compressed air. It has a base efficiency of 40%%, i.e. it takes 100 FE to generate 40 mL of compressed air. Speed Upgrades will reduce this efficiency slightly.

gui.tooltip.block.pneumaticcraft.pneumat:
Converts compressed air into Forge Energy (compatible with RF and many other mods' energy). It has a base efficiency of 40%%, i.e. 100mL of air be used to generate 40 FE. Speed Upgrades will reduce this efficiency slightly.

gui.tooltip.block.pneumaticcraft.securit:
When you want to protect an area from others messing with your stuff, you can use this machine to prevent other players from interacting with (or breaking) every block within its range. You can whitelist friends by adding them in the Trusted Players tab.
Read the manual (Patchouli required) for detailed information on how to set up the network for best results, but do note that the Security Station is not 100%% immune from being hacked by a hostile player. You can do a dry-run test of the network's effectiveness with the Test button.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.air_grat:
§9Formula: Range(blocks) = 4.0 x pressure(bar), or -16 x pressure(bar) if vacuum

§bThis module will repel or attract any entity within range dependent on whether pressure is positive or negative, respectively, and will attempt to insert items into any adjacent inventory.  Can also be used to cool Heat Sinks.

gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.flow_det:

§bThis module emits a redstone signal, the strength of which depends on how much air is travelling through the tube.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.logistic: §bThis module communicates with other Logistics Modules on connected tubes to perform logistics tasks on any inventories or tanks it is pointing at, which are fitted with a Logistic Frame. It uses pressure from the tube to do so.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.pressure:
§9Formula: Redstone = 2.0 x pressure(bar)

§bThis module emits a redstone signal, the strength of which depends on the tube's pressure.

When upgraded with a Module Expansion Card, the threshold can be configured precisely via GUI.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.redstone:
§bThis module transmits redstone signals to other Redstone Modules on connected tubes. Right-click with any dye to set the channel; right-click with a wrench to toggle between input and output.

Upgrade with a Module Expansion Card for extra signal processing operations.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.regulato:
§bThis module limits the pressure allowed on its low side based on the redstone signal it receives. No signal = 4.9 bar, a full signal = 0 bar (no air allowed through), and other signal levels are interpolated. Air is always allowed to travel "backwards" through the Regulator, making it usable as a one-way valve.
When upgraded with a Module Expansion Card, the threshold can be configured precisely via GUI.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.safety_t:
§bThis module will vent high pressure air if the tube pressure reaches 4.9 bar (19.9 for Advanced Pressure Tubes). Although this prevents explosions, released air is energy loss and wastes fuel.

When upgraded with a Module Expansion Card, the threshold can be configured precisely via GUI.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.thermost:
§bThis module transmits redstone signals to Redstone Modules on connected tubes based on temperature of facing block. Right-click with any dye to set the channel.

Upgrade with a Module Expansion Card for extra signal processing operations.
gui.tooltip.item.pneumaticcraft.vacuum_m: §bActs just like a Vacuum Pump, but as a module. Takes pressure at the wide (green) end, and removes it at the narrow (red) end. Install a Module Expansion Card to increase operation speed. Apply a Redstone Signal to prevent operation.

item.tempad.knowledge_projector.card_cra: Location Cards are created from Iron Ingots and any Dye. The recipe produces 4 Location Cards. Alternatively one may substitute the iron for an ingot of %s and receive 16 cards from the same recipe.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.card_usa: To write location data to a card, a %s or %s is required at the correct coordinates or a standard issue %s with the coordinates already saved inside. Right-clicking the card onto a %s or %s will link the card to the device. Right-clicking the card onto the information panel for a location saved inside the %s will write the location data to the card.

Written cards can be used to supply location data to a %s or a %s. Cards obtained from other players only function with the %s if placed into a carried %s, however all cards can be freely used with the %s.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.cell_usa: Empty Chronon Cells can be charged slowly over time if carried alongside a %s or a %s, or they can be placed inside a %s. Charged Chronon Cells will transfer their stored Chronons to all carried devices automatically, so long as they are all present in the main inventory or curio slots. Chronon Cells hold {X} Chronons.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.chronoma: Chronomarks are crafted from a Block of Iron, Iron Ingots, ingots of %s, an Ender Pearl, and a block of Tinted Glass.

The Chronomark is a stationary block used to generate exact spatial coordinates and provide them to other devices. As an upgrade over %s, Chronomarks allow for an offset of up to %s blocks to be specified in case the user wants to mount the device on a high ceiling or bury the device under the floor. They also allow for more user filtering options.

To write data to a %s, place the Chronomark and right-click it with a %s. The card will then be written and can be used with %s. The %s displays Chronomarks and %ss owned by the user automatically, but written %ss can be shared with others.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.chronome: Chronometers can be created from any basic Clock, along with a few extra components. Also required will be a block of Tinted Glass, ingots of %s, and a %s.

Kept in the main inventory or a curio slot, a Chronometer or %s will invert the temporal decay of local background radiation to synthesize Chronons, which are then distributed to all carried devices or storage cells automatically, so long as they are all present in the main inventory or curio slots.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.chronon_: Chronon Batteries can be created with %s, Iron Ingots, %ss, and Amethyst Shards, to power multiversal devices, and are the ideal way to carry Chronons on the go.
Chronon Batteries are devices for storing Chronons made from smaller cells. They hold more Chronons than individual %ss.

Empty Chronon Batteries can be charged slowly over time if carried alongside a %s or a %s, or they can be placed inside a %s. Charged Chronon Batteries will transfer their stored Chronons to all carried devices automatically, so long as they are all present in the main inventory or curio slots. Chronon Batteries hold %s Chronons.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.chronong: Chronon Generators can be created from any basic Clock, along with a block of Glass, Iron Ingots, and a %s

Kept in the main inventory or a curio slot, a Chronon Generator or %s will invert the temporal decay of local background radiation to synthesize Chronons, which are then distributed to all carried devices or storage cells automatically, so long as they are all present in the main inventory or curio slots.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.location: The Location Broadcaster allow lost agents to be found and rescued by agents with specially upgraded %s.
If a Location Broadcaster is carried in the inventory or curio slot and is turned on, the carrier will appearin the list of possible teleports for %s with the Teleport to Players upgrade.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.marker_u: To write data to a %s, place the Timedoor Marker and right-click it with a %s. The card will then be written and can be used with the %s. The %s displays Timedoor Markers and %ss owned by the user automatically, but %ss linked to devices can be shared with others.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.metronom: Once booted, the Metronome will begin to generate Chronons into its own internal battery, which holds %s Chronons. Right-clicking the device will bring up the interface, where devices can be placed to store Chronons via the left-hand slots or take Chronons via the right-hand slots. Additionally, the Metronome is coded to the user’s temporal aura, and may be locked to prevent unauthorized access via the lock button in the upper right. It is locked by default.
Metronomes are crafted with Ingots of %s, Chronon Batteries, and an Ender Chest.

Generally, Metronomes cannot be charged within the inventory, and instead need to be placed into the world. There is an initial charge of Chronons needed to boot the device and gain access to its functionality after it is placed. This boot charge can be provided from a %s or %s in hand by crouch-right-clicking the Metronome.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.projecto: Timedoor Projectors are crafted from Copper Ingots, a Glass block, an Ender Pearl, a %s and Blocks of Iron.

When a standard issue %s is unavailable, rudimentary versions of the device can be crafted using materials on hand. The Timedoor Projector is the most basic device capable of allowing teleportation via Timedoors.

Timedoor Projectors allow for the creation of Timedoors to spatial coordinates read from %ss. These can be loaded into the device by right-clicking the card onto the Timedoor Projector while it is either in the inventory or placed in the world, or by right-clicking a card in the inventory while holding the projector with the cursor. Cards can be retrieved from the device by either right-clicking it on an empty inventory space, or by right-clicking the device where it is placed in the world.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.screenin: Screening Devices are crafted with a block of Tinted Glass, an Emerald, a measure of Redstone Dust, a Compass, and an ingot of %s.
The Screening Device is an advanced version of the %s that features more advanced filtering capability.

On a surface level, the Screening Device provides the same functionality as the %s, allowing users with upgraded %s to open Timedoors directly to their location. Additionally, the Screening Device can also filter who is given this permission based on available and compatible team or guild frameworks. Holding the device and right-click using it will cycle the device through its available modes.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.tempad_a: When docked on a %s, the terminal provides access to the Portal Setup app, allowing for selection of a destination from the user’s docked Tempad, and for precision tweaks to the opened Timedoor’s position and rotation (plus or minus %s blocks from the default position). This app is not available without docking the Tempad. Please see the %s entry for more information.

Opening the Teleport app will present the user with a list of locations saved in the device, as well as the %ss or %ss owned by the user. Clicking these entries will populate the info panel to the right of the list, and enable the teleport button. Clicking the Teleport button will consume Chronons and generate a Timedoor to the location specified in the entry.

When a location is selected from the list, and the info panel to the right is populated, two additional buttons display at the bottom of the panel. The pin button will pin the location to the top of the list. Only one location may be pinned at a time. The X button will delete the location from the list. A %s right-clicked onto this information panel will be written with the location data from the saved location.

With a %s docked inside the Tempad, access is gained to the Travel Timeline app. This expands the functionality of the docked %s and gives more granular control, allowing the user to move back along to more points along their timeline instead of being limited to major events.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.tempad_c: The Tempad is crafted with blocks of Tinted Glass, a piece of Nether Quartz, an Ender Pearl, a Redstone Lamp, ingots of %s, and a %s.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.tempad_o: The standard issue Tempad is the single most powerful piece of technology covered in this database. A Tempad can create Timedoors to any coordinates saved in the device, as well as access a docked %s to allow the user to view and move along their personal timeline.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.tempad_t: Timedoors consume Chronons from the Tempad upon generation and appear for a set amount of time before closing automatically. %ss given a constant redstone signal will open a door indefinitely for a continuous Chronon cost.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.tempad_u: Location data can be added to the Tempad for teleporting via the New Location app. To use %ss with the Tempad, please see the %s.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.time_twi: It is crafted with ingots of %s, blocks of Tinted Glass, a %s, and an Ender Pearl.

If more granularity in timeline events is required, the Time Twister can be docked with a %s to provide access to the Travel Timeline app. The Time Twister is docked by right-clicking it onto a %s in the inventory, or by right-clicking a %s onto the Time Twister. This also provides the benefit of carrying the Time Twister without it taking an extra inventory slot.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.wallet_c: Card Wallets can be crafted with Copper Ingots, Leather, and a blank %s.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.wallet_u: Right click the wallet in hand to open its storage. %ss may be placed in the storage for safe-keeping to keep the inventory from becoming too cluttered.

Once the user obtains a standard %s, Cards inside the wallet are automatically added to the %s’s location list if they are placed inside a carried wallet. Note that this is unnecessary for a %s or a %s owned by the user, as these devices are already added to the user’s %s. What this does enable, however, is the continued sharing of location cards between users, and being able to access these shared cards via the %s’s interface.

Only one Card Wallet can provide locations to the user’s %s at a given time. Priority is placed on the curio slot if available, then hotbar slots from left to right, then inventory slots from left to right, top to bottom.
item.tempad.knowledge_projector.workstat: It can be crafted with blocks of Tinted Glass, Copper Ingots, ingots of %s, and a piece of Nether Quartz.
The Workstation is a stationary computer terminal that allows the user to accomplish various tasks when a %s is placed on the docking pad.

Docking a %s by right-clicking it onto the docking pad unlocks the cassette slot at the back to allow the use of Upgrade Tapes. Right-clicking an Upgrade Tape into the cassette slot applies the upgrade on the tape to the docked %s, provided the specific upgrade isn’t already present on the device.

When a %s is docked on the docking pad, the terminal to the left is also unlocked, allowing the user to set up a stationary teleportation device. The usage of the Workstation in this way is similar to the %s, in that it accepts a redstone signal from any side and creates a Timedoor for the user.

Right-clicking on the terminal, however, opens a new Portal Setup app, allowing for selection of a destination from the user’s docked %s, and for precision tweaks to the opened Timedoor’s position and rotation (plus or minus %s blocks in any direction from the default position). Additionally, if a constant redstone signal is applied the Timedoors will remain open until the signal stops, after which it will resume its normal countdown to close.

jei.reliquary.description.magicbane:
The Magicbane is an artifact athame from Nethack I decided to do a small tribute to.

With a durability of 16, it's one of the most easily breakable weapons one can acquire. When striking you have a 50%% chance of inflicting one of the following status ailments: Confusion, Blindness, Slowness, Weakness

Also, with each enchantment on the blade, the enchantment's level is added to the total damage. So a Fire Aspect II Magicbane would deal its default, plus 2 damage.

It's officially made of gold, for Touchstone of Midas purposes, and is thus enchantable as gold.
